phase: ## Phase 1G: Grouping of old articles (Tasks 1.G1 to 1.G5)
summary: PASS. The plan-specified CLI contract holds in live runs. The six options parse, and the defaults match the plan. Given paths resolve against the working directory. Parse errors print the message, then the usage, on stderr, and exit 2. The usage names all six options. A run writes exactly the two given files and exits 0. Importing the script prints nothing and sets no exit code. g3-crosscheck exits 2 with the exact message for a missing environment variable. Two error paths outside the plan's list exit 1 with a raw stack trace. One path lacks the --inventory option (F1, Major). The other path names a missing inventory file (F2, Nit). F1 is a regression against afbfcf0e.
nonblocking_findings: F1 [Major] review-c: dashboard/scripts/plan-dedup.ts:196 and 293-299 - a run without --inventory exits 1 with a path.resolve TypeError and prints no message and no usage. The usage marks --inventory required at line 55, and the base afbfcf0e printed usage and exited 2. Rationale: the exit-code contract names only 0 and 2, and parseDedupArgs declares ok:false for bad input instead of throwing. Owner: Green. Fix: fail in parseDedupArgs when --inventory is absent, print message and usage, and exit 2. Note: Review A F1 names the same defect; one fix closes both.

F2 [Nit] review-c: dashboard/scripts/plan-dedup.ts:300 - a run whose --inventory names a missing file exits 1 with a raw ENOENT stack. Line 183 answers a missing --printed file with a message, then usage, and exit 2. Rationale: the plan promises no behavior for this input and the base behaved the same, so the gap is error-response consistency only. Owner: Green. Fix: check the inventory file in main, print 'inventory file not found: <the given path>', then usage, and exit 2.
